title: Volume of Square and Rectangular Pyramids
seo_title: Grade 7 Volume of Pyramids Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 7)
standard_text: Explore inductively the volume of square and rectangular pyramids using rectangular prisms, leading to the identification of the formula; estimate volumes of square and rectangular pyramids; solve problems involving volumes of square or rectangular pyramids.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 volume of pyramids worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: square and rectangular pyramids, the one-third rule, missing heights, estimates and problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A pyramid is one third of the prism with the same base and height.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A pyramid fits into a prism with the same base and height 3 times. So V = 13 × base area × height.
  • Square pyramid: V = 13s²h. Rectangular pyramid: V = 13lwh.
  • The height is measured straight up from the base to the top, not along a slanted face.
  • To estimate, round the measures to easy numbers first.

Examples

Example

Base 6 cm × 6 cm, height 10 cm

13 × 36 × 10

Answer: 120 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the one thirdA pyramid is one third of the prism.
Using the slant heightUse the vertical height.
Two dimensions onlyVolume needs length, width and height.

items.q: A pyramid has a volume of 72 cm³. A prism has the same base and height. What is the volume of the prism?
items.e: A prism holds 3 times as much: 3 × 72 = 216 cm³.

items.q: A pyramid and a prism have the same base and the same height. How many pyramids full of sand fill the prism?
items.e: The volume of a pyramid is ⅓ of the prism with the same base and height, so 3 pyramids fill it.

items.q: Which formula gives the volume of a pyramid with base area B and height h?
items.e: A pyramid is one third of a prism with the same base and height: V = ⅓Bh.
